hero.eyebrow: Skills assessment that shows its working
hero.title: Hire for what people can do.
hero.sub: Candidates spend a realistic week at a fictional company. Every answer narrows what we know about them, and every score rests on their own words. Your team decides.

figure.label: One skill, estimated scene by scene: the range narrows from the whole scale to 3.6–4.2, and the estimate settles at 3.9.

how.label: How it works
how.title: A realistic week. Evidence you can check.
how.intro: Paste a job description. Aalim finds the skills the role needs, flags requirements that could exclude people unfairly, and builds the week around them.

week.title: A week at a fictional company
week.body: About 50 minutes of messages, decisions, documents and conversations. Each answer shapes the next scene, so the time goes where it tells you most.

range.title: Every answer narrows the range
range.body: Aalim starts unsure and says so. Each scene adds evidence until the estimate is tight enough to trust.

evidence.title: Every score shows its working
evidence.body: The candidate’s own words sit under every score, with the questions to ask next. Your team makes the decision.

scene.subject: Port delay: the Henderson order
scene.message: Two of our three trucks are stuck at the port. The Henderson order is due at 4pm and they’ve already complained twice this month. What do you do first?
scene.adaptive: New, because of the last answer
scene.reply: I’d call Henderson before ten and offer a split delivery: half today from the Riyadh stock, the rest first thing tomorrow

evidence.answerStart: I’d call Henderson before ten and offer a split delivery:
evidence.answerEvidence: half today from the Riyadh stock, the rest first thing tomorrow,

report.label: The report

report.body: Role fit with a confidence, a range for every skill, the candidate’s own words under every score, and the questions to ask in the interview.

frame.label: A candidate report in Aalim

frame.ask1: Tell me about a plan you promised that couldn’t hold. Who did you tell first?

hire.body: Compare candidates on what they did in the scenarios, not how well they write a CV.

grow.body: Find your level, practise where it matters and get feedback that names what to do next. Private to you.

grow.expert: Check who else the delay affects before you promise a new time.

team.body: With each person’s consent, see your team’s strengths, gaps and who is ready to lead.

team.heatCaption: Six people across five skill areas. Darker is stronger.

trust.label: Trust
trust.title: Built to be fair, and to stay fair.

people.title: People decide

fairness.title: Checked for fairness

privacy.title: Data that belongs to people

gallery.title: Design system
gallery.intro: Every Aalim component, built on the design tokens. Switch theme, language and numerals in the header: every specimen should hold up in all of them.

sectionNotes.foundations: Colour, type, space, shape, icons and motion.
sectionNotes.controls: Buttons are verbs. Errors say what to do next.
sectionNotes.navigation: One soft shadow, for floating layers only.
sectionNotes.feedback: Every screen has designed empty, loading and error states.
sectionNotes.assessment: The candidate's world: materials look real, nothing counts down loudly.
sectionNotes.report: Levels use one hue, never red and green. Every score carries a range.

foundations.typeNote: Inter for Latin, IBM Plex Sans Arabic for Arabic. Body line height 1.5, headings 1.2.
foundations.shapeNote: Radius 8 for controls, 12 for cards. One shadow, for popovers.
foundations.motionNote: 150–250 ms, ease-out, only to explain a change. Off when reduced motion is set.
foundations.motionPanel: Panels fade and rise 4 px as they open. Nothing bounces.

people.title: You kept people in mind

fairness.title: Help us check that our assessments are fair (optional)

fairness.thanks: Thank you. Your answers are stored separately from your assessment.

ai.title: How AI is used in this assessment
ai.intro: You have a right to know where AI is involved. This is all of it.

does.world: Writes the fictional company and its scenes, and adapts them to your answers.
does.roleplay: Plays the colleagues you talk to in conversations.
does.scoring: Scores the content of your answers against written descriptions of each skill level.
does.report: Drafts the report, quoting your own words as evidence.

never.decide: Decide whether you are hired, or reject anyone.
never.face: Look at your face, or analyse your voice, tone, accent or emotions.
never.integrity: Treat a paste or a switched tab as cheating. These are context for the reviewer, never a verdict.

ai.decide: People at {org} read the report and make every decision. They can change any level, and every change is recorded with a reason.
ai.choice: The scenes adapt using automated scoring either way. If you ask for a human review, a person at {org} must read your answers and confirm or change every level before the report can be shared or exported.

newPage.description: Paste the job description. Aalim drafts the role summary, the technical skills and how much each area matters. You review and edit it all before publishing.
newPage.jdHint: Include responsibilities and requirements. Aalim also flags requirements that may be discriminatory or irrelevant.
newPage.jdPlaceholder:
Senior Data Analyst

We're looking for…
newPage.modeOffline: Analysed with Aalim's built-in role templates
newPage.analysingBody: This usually takes a few seconds.

errors.jdLength: Paste the full job description (at least 80 characters).

newPage.exampleJd:
Customer Success Team Lead

We're looking for a Customer Success Team Lead to run a team of six account managers looking after 300 business customers across the Gulf.

What you'll do
- Lead, coach and plan the work of six account managers
- Own renewals and spot accounts at risk early, using usage data and customer conversations
- Handle escalations with senior customer stakeholders
- Work with product and support to fix the problems customers raise most
- Report on retention and satisfaction to the Head of Customer Experience

What you bring
- 5+ years in customer success or account management, including 2 leading people
- Comfortable with numbers: you can find the story in a renewal forecast
- Calm, clear communication in difficult conversations
- Arabic and English

method.p1: The candidate worked through one continuous story at a fictional company. The assessment adapted as they answered: it formed hypotheses about their strengths and gaps, tested each in different-looking situations, and raised the difficulty to find their ceiling.
method.p2: Each answer was scored against written descriptions of five levels for each sub-skill. Every score quotes the candidate's own words. Length, grammar, accent and fluency are not scored.
method.ai: Scenarios and scoring used Claude. Important answers were scored twice independently; where the passes disagreed by more than a level, a third pass decided ({n} answers were double-scored).
method.offline: This session used Aalim's curated, human-reviewed scenarios and its built-in scorer. Confidence is deliberately conservative.
method.p3: Levels are estimates with ranges. They become more certain as the same skill shows up consistently across different situations.

brandbook.title: Brand book
brandbook.metaDescription: Range, the Aalim brand: the idea, the mark, lockups, colour, type, the narrowing motif, voice and files, in English and Arabic.

cover.statement: Every answer narrows what we know about a person. The mark is that process: wide bands of uncertainty tightening, step by step, into one point. It also reads as an A. Ink, bone and a single vermilion signal.

idea.title: The idea
idea.body1: An assessment starts out knowing almost nothing: the person could be anywhere on the scale. Each answer is evidence, and each piece of evidence rules something out. The band of plausible levels tightens until what is left is an estimate we can stand behind, with the person’s own words underneath it.
idea.body2: Range draws exactly that. Wide bands below, narrower above, and one vermilion point at the top: the estimate. Centre the bands and they stack into an A, for Aalim.

figure.after: After {count, plural, one {# answer} other {# answers}}
figure.caption: One skill, measured. The band is where the level could be, and it narrows with every answer.
figure.centred: Centre the same drawing and it becomes the mark.

idea.nameBody: In Arabic, the same four letters spell ʿālim, someone who knows a subject deeply, and ʿālam, a world. Aalim builds a world for each person, a realistic week at a fictional company, and finds out what they know in it.
idea.usage: Write Aalim in English text and عالِم in Arabic. The capitals AALIM belong to the wordmark.

exact.title: Exact
exact.body: Measured and aligned. If a line is there, it means something.

warm.title: Warm
warm.body: Bone, not white; stone, not grey. A product about people should feel made by people.

honest.title: Honest about certainty
honest.body: Ranges, not verdicts. We show how sure we are, and why.

mark.title: The mark
mark.body: Every row is 11 units tall, 3.5 apart. The bands step in by 8 units a side, 58, 42, 26, and the fourth row is the step after that: a band too narrow to be a band, the dot. The ends are fully round. A line through the band ends meets just above the dot: the legs of the A.
mark.figureLabel: The mark on its 64-unit grid, with its measurements
mark.colourBody: The bands take the opposite of the ground: ink on bone, bone on ink. The dot is vermilion, always, except where only one colour can be printed.

lockups.title: Lockups
lockups.lede: One drawing, six arrangements. Use the files; never rebuild them.

english.body: English-only layouts and tight horizontal spaces.

mono.body: Stamps, embossing and one-colour print. The dot joins the bands.

reverse.name: Reversed
reverse.body: On ink. Bands and letters in bone; the dot stays vermilion.

tile.name: App tile
tile.body: The mark at 70% on an ink square with a 22.5% corner. The vermilion tile is for marketing only.

lockups.wordmarkBody: AALIM in Archivo Expanded ExtraBold, tracked open a little. عالم in Beiruti Black, never tracked, its alif rising 18% above the Latin capitals so both read at the same size. Baselines align, and a hairline at 22% ink separates them. Every file is outlined, so no font is needed to open it.

space.title: Space and size
space.lede: Give the logo room, and never draw it smaller than it can be read.
space.clearBody: Keep x clear on every side, where x is the height of the capitals in AALIM. Around the mark on its own, keep half its width. Text, edges and other logos stay outside.
space.minBody: Shown at actual size. Smaller than this, the bands close up: use the mark alone.
space.print: In print: the horizontal lockup at least 30 mm wide, the mark at least 5 mm.

misuse.title: Misuse
misuse.lede: The logo is a drawing, not a typeface. Don’t change it.

items.recolour: Recolour the bands or the dot
items.ground: Put it on vermilion or a busy picture
items.retype: Retype the wordmark in another font
items.redraw: Redraw the bands or change their steps

colour.title: Colour
colour.lede: Ink, bone and a single vermilion signal. The neutrals are warm stone so the vermilion belongs. Everything is flat: no gradients, no glows.

ink.name: Ink
ink.role: Text, the logo, primary actions and the one hero panel on each screen.

bone.name: Bone
bone.role: The canvas. White cards sit on it, edged with a hairline.

signal.name: Vermilion
signal.role: The signal: the estimate, range bands, focus and at most one call to action per screen. Ink text on it, never bone.

evidence.name: Evidence
evidence.role: The highlighter behind a person’s own words. Never decoration.

colour.stoneBody: Warm neutrals for secondary text, hairlines and borders.
colour.pairsBody: WCAG ratios for every pairing of the core colours. AA needs 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for large text (24 px, or 19 px bold) and graphics. Every pairing used in the product is tested in code.
colour.ruleBody: Vermilion is a ground or a graphic. Text on it is ink. On bone it is never small text: at {ratio}:1 it passes only for large display and shapes.

type.title: Typography
type.lede: Archivo, wide and heavy, for what we declare. Beiruti for Arabic display. IBM Plex for everything people read and use.

plex.name: IBM Plex Sans
plex.role: Reading and interface, in both scripts
plex.sampleEn: Strongest in diagnosing problems. Ask about stakeholder management in the interview: the evidence there is thin.
plex.sampleAr: أقوى ما يكون في تشخيص المشكلات. اسأل عن إدارة الأطراف المعنية في المقابلة، فالأدلة على ذلك قليلة.

type.widthBody: Archivo runs from condensed to expanded. Range uses the widest setting for display, so even short words carry weight.

samples.title: Prioritising under pressure
samples.body: Called the client before ten and offered a split delivery.
samples.label: Role fit

arabicRules: Arabic display is Beiruti, never Archivo. Arabic has no capitals and is never letter-spaced: tracking breaks the joins.
Give it room: line height 1.65 for reading and about 1.3 for display, so dots and marks never touch.
Set Arabic display a step larger than the Latin beside it. In the logo, عالم rises 18% above the capitals.
Use the fonts’ own weights. Never stretch, slant or fake bold Arabic.
Mirror the layout, not the content: direction, alignment and range bands flip; logos, numbers, links and code don’t.
Latin digits by default; Arabic-Indic digits are a personal setting. Use Arabic punctuation: ، ؛ ؟
latinRules: Capitals for display and labels only. Titles and sentences are in sentence case.
Archivo never sets running text. Reading is Plex, at 16 px or more.
Labels are tracked open by 14%. Display is set tight and never tracked.

motif.title: The narrowing
motif.lede: The mark’s idea, at work in the product.
motif.bandsBody: Every estimate is a band on the 1–5 scale: wide while the evidence is thin, narrow once it settles. The dot is the estimate and the tick is the level the role expects. Bands are vermilion, horizontal and always data.
motif.heroBody: Each screen has one filled panel, in ink, holding its one verdict. The mark’s bands sit faintly in its corner, and the dot keeps its vermilion.

hero.body: Strongest in problem diagnosis. Confirm stakeholder management in the interview.

motif.cornerLabel: Corner mark: bands at 9%, dot in vermilion
motif.openerBody: A hairline with a short vermilion tick at its start opens a section. In Arabic the tick sits on the right.
motif.evidenceBody: The person’s own words, marked like a reviewer’s highlighter. Only verbatim quotes get it.
motif.evidenceSample: Before I reply to the client, I’d check
motif.evidenceMark: whether the delay affects the other two orders on the same route.
motif.rule: Bands run horizontally, wider means less certain, and the dot is the conclusion. Outside the logo and the hero corner, bands only ever show data.

ui.title: Interface
ui.lede: The brand in the product, built from the same components.
ui.buttonsBody: Ink is the action colour. The vermilion signal button is the screen’s one call to action, if it has one.
ui.quoteBefore: I’d agree a stop rule with the team:
ui.quoteMark: if we see more than five duplicates in a day, we pause and roll back.

voice.title: Voice
voice.lede: Exact, warm and honest about certainty. We sound like a careful colleague, not a machine or a salesperson.

specific.title: Specific over impressive
specific.body: “Spotted that station 2 closes at noon”, not “strong analytical skills”.

ranges.title: Numbers with ranges and reasons
ranges.body: Give the level, the range and why. Never a bare percentage.

calm.title: Calm
calm.body: No exclamation marks, urgency tricks or hype words like “revolutionary” or “AI-powered”.

verbs.title: Verbs on buttons
verbs.body: Sentence case and active voice. The button says what happens: “Publish”, then “Published”.

candidates.title: To candidates
candidates.body: Calm and reassuring, clear about their data.
candidates.example: Take the time you need. Your answers save as you type.

teams.title: To hiring teams
teams.body: Precise and brief. Lead with what to do.

growth.title: To people growing
growth.example: You named the trade-off. An expert would also check who else the delay affects.

examples: You were strongest when weighing evidence.
Scenarios adapt to each answer, and every score quotes the person’s own words.
Partial fit. Below the expected level in management: explore it in the interview.

downloads.title: Downloads
downloads.lede: Outlined vectors (no fonts needed) and PNG renders, generated from the brand fonts by npm run brand:assets.

footer.line: Range is the Aalim brand. Version 1.0, November 2026.

invite.subject: {org} invites you to an assessment for {role}
invite.preheader: About {minutes} minutes of realistic work scenarios. You can pause between chapters.
invite.headingNamed: {name}, you’re invited to show what you can do
invite.heading: You’re invited to show what you can do
invite.p1: {org} has invited you to a work-scenario assessment for the {role} role. It takes about {minutes} minutes, and you can pause between chapters.
invite.p2: There are no trick questions. You’ll spend a week at a fictional company: reading messages, making decisions and writing replies. People at {org} make the hiring decision; the assessment gives them evidence.
invite.note: This link is personal and expires in {days} days. You can choose extra time or larger text before you begin.

renew.subject: Your new assessment link for {role}
renew.preheader: A fresh link to continue your assessment.
renew.heading: Here’s your new link
renew.p1: Here is a new link to your assessment for the {role} role at {org}. It expires in {days} days.

team.subject: {manager} invites you to a team development assessment
team.preheader: A development tool, not a performance review. You see your report first.
team.heading: Help {team} grow, on your terms
team.p1: {manager} has invited you to a team development assessment for {team} at {org}.
team.p2: This is a development tool, not a performance review. You see your own report first. With fewer than five people, your manager sees only anonymised team totals, and never your answers unless you choose to share them.

reset.subject: Reset your Aalim password
reset.preheader: The link expires in one hour.
reset.heading: Choose a new password
reset.p1: Use the button below to choose a new password. The link expires in one hour.
reset.note: If you didn’t ask for this, you can ignore this email. Your password won’t change.

report.preheader: Your strengths and what to develop, with quotes from your own answers.
report.heading: Your report is ready
report.p1: {org} has shared your assessment report for the {role} role with you. It shows your strengths and what to develop, with quotes from your own answers.

rep.subject: Your 2-minute rep is ready
rep.heading: Ready when you are, {name}
rep.p1: Today's rep is one quick decision on {skill}, set in your kind of work. It takes about two minutes.
rep.note: You asked for this reminder. Turn it off any time from your Grow page.

repStreak.start: A good day to start a streak.

interview.title: Interview kit
interview.description: Questions for {name} ({role}) on what the assessment couldn't settle. Rate each answer as you go.
interview.pendingBody: The kit is built from the report. It appears here as soon as the report is ready.
interview.blind: Rate before you look: the assessment's levels and other interviewers' scorecards appear after you submit yours. {n, plural, =0 {No scorecards yet.} one {1 scorecard submitted.} other {# scorecards submitted.}}
interview.revealed: Your scorecard is in: the assessment's levels and the team's ratings are now shown.
interview.notRated: Not rated: leave it if you didn't cover this
interview.notePlaceholder: What they said and did (their words where you can)
interview.apart: More than a level apart: discuss in the debrief
interview.overallBody: Base it on this interview. You'll see how it compares with the assessment once you submit.
interview.summaryPlaceholder: The two or three things that most shaped your view
interview.error: Couldn't save your scorecard. Rate at least one area, choose a recommendation and write a short summary.
interview.debriefBody: {n} scorecards in. Start with where people disagree.
interview.debriefSolo: Only your scorecard so far. Compare it with the assessment below.
interview.disagreeTitle: {n, plural, one {1 area to discuss} other {# areas to discuss}}
interview.disagreeBody: An interview rating sits more than a level away from the assessment on: {skills}. Look at the evidence together before deciding.
interview.agree: Interview ratings sit within the assessment's ranges.
